Authors: Zoheb Khan Modified: January 24, 2026 Compiled: May 9, 2026 Environment: R version 4.6.0 (2026-04-24); Bioconductor 3.23 Dependencies: base64enc {0.1.6}; BiocManager {1.30.27}; bookdown {0.46}; ggplot2 {4.0.3}; ggrepel {0.9.8}; GO.db {3.23.1}; jsonlite {2.0.0}; RColorBrewer {1.1.3}; scales {1.4.0}; svglite {2.2.2}; systemfonts {1.3.2} Source: repository root ( . ) 1 Overview This workflow provides sourceable R plotting functions for precomputed Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) results. It does not run DESeq2, build ranked gene lists, or calculate enrichment. Those steps should stay in the analysis pipeline that produced the GSEA result table. Rendered tutorial: https://zohebkhan1.github.io/gsea-waterfall/ The plotting functions generate four figure types: ranked positive and negative NES waterfall plots a symmetric GSEA volcano plot directional half-volcano plots comparative NES scatterplots across two GSEA contrasts The worked example uses GO biological-process GSEA results from GSE122380 cardiomyocyte differentiation contrasts. The example input CSVs are deliberately small and contain only the columns needed for plotting. 2 Get The Functions Download only the plotting functions from GitHub: # set the raw github function path base_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZohebKhan1/gsea-waterfall/main/functions" download.file ( paste0 (base_url, "/gsea_waterfall_plot.R" ), "gsea_waterfall_plot.R" ) download.file ( paste0 (base_url, "/gsea_volcano_plot.R" ), "gsea_volcano_plot.R" ) download.file ( paste0 (base_url, "/gsea_half_volcano_plot.R" ), "gsea_half_volcano_plot.R" ) download.file ( paste0 (base_url, "/gsea_nes_scatter_plot.R" ), "gsea_nes_scatter_plot.R" ) source ( "gsea_waterfall_plot.R" ) source ( "gsea_volcano_plot.R" ) source ( "gsea_half_volcano_plot.R" ) source ( "gsea_nes_scatter_plot.R" ) Cloning the repository downloads the public tutorial source, plotting functions, minimal example CSVs, rendered assets, and GitHub Pages site. Private inputs, full result tables, reference folders, internal scripts, and local agent files are excluded by .gitignore . 3 Input Table Each plot function expects a precomputed GSEA result table. Use this header: Column Required Meaning go_description yes GO term name NES yes normalized enrichment score pval yes nominal GSEA p-value padj yes adjusted p-value These four columns are the only columns users need for the plotting workflow shown here. 4 Waterfall Plots Use plot_gsea_waterfall() for a ranked view of enriched GO terms in one NES direction. Terms can be ranked by NES , padj , or pvalue . Labels can be selected by exact term name, GO ID when available, plotted rank, or automatic rank-based selection. term_groups and label_terms are intentionally separate. term_groups defines broad biological categories for point colors; label_terms defines the smaller set of GO terms that should receive text labels. By default, category matching uses exact GO IDs and text seeds. Set include_descendants = TRUE only when category seeds include GO IDs and GO offspring should be included through GO.db . 4.1 Positive NES waterfall # define color groups positive_term_groups <- list ( "Ion channel" = c ( "Calcium" , "Sodium" , "Potassium" , "Ion" , "Voltage" , "Channel" , "electrical" , "Action potential" , "transmembrane" , "conduction" ), "Metabolism" = c ( "Metabolic" , "Metabolism" , "Electron transport chain" , "Mitochondria" , "Mitochondrial" , "Oxidative" , "Phosphorylation" , "ATP" , "lipid" , "biosynthetic" , "respiration" ), "Muscle contraction" = c ( "Muscle contraction" , "Muscle cell differentiation" , "Striated" , "Sarcomere" , "Myofibril" , "Actin" , "Muscle" ), "Heart development" = c ( "atrial" , "ventricular" , "heart" , "cardiac" ) ) # define labeled terms positive_label_terms <- c ( "myofibril assembly" , "cardiac muscle contraction" , "cardiac muscle cell action potential" , "calcium-mediated signaling" , "electron transport chain" , "muscle cell differentiation" , "ATP metabolic process" , "cardiac cell development" , "cardiac chamber morphogenesis" , "muscle contraction" , "cardiac conduction" , "cardiac muscle cell contraction" , "heart growth" , "cardiac atrium development" , "heart trabecula morphogenesis" ) # plot ranked positive terms positive_waterfall <- plot_gsea_waterfall ( gsea_results = gsea_cardiomyocyte_vs_mesoderm, direction = "positive" , top_n = 100 , rank_by = "NES" , x_label = "Ranked GO terms by NES for Cardiomyocyte vs. Mesoderm" , label_n = 10 , label_terms = positive_label_terms, term_groups = positive_term_groups, category_n = 4 ) Figure 1. Positive NES GO biological-process waterfall for Cardiomyocyte vs. Mesoderm. Terms are ranked by NES, colored by manually defined cardiac-relevant GO term groups, and labeled with selected high-priority terms. 4.2 Negative NES waterfall # define negative color groups negative_term_groups <- list ( "Ribosomal" = c ( "ribosome" , "ribosomal" , "spliceosomal" , "rRNA" , "RNA" ), "Mitosis" = c ( "Mitosis" , "Meiosis" , "Nuclear division" , "cell cycle" , "telomere" , "spindle" , "Mitotic" , "Meiotic" ), "DNA replication" = c ( "chromosome" , "DNA" , "base" , "repair" , "DNA-" ) ) # set negative group colors negative_term_group_colors <- c ( "Ribosomal" = "#377EB8" , "Mitosis" = "#984EA3" , "DNA replication" = "#E41A1C" ) negative_waterfall <- plot_gsea_waterfall ( gsea_results = gsea_cardiomyocyte_vs_mesoderm, direction = "negative" , top_n = 100 , rank_by = "NES" , x_label = "Ranked GO terms by NES for Cardiomyocyte vs. Mesoderm" , label_n = 10 , term_groups = negative_term_groups, term_group_colors = negative_term_group_colors ) Figure 2. Negative NES GO biological-process waterfall for the same contrast. The selected groups highlight ribosomal, mitotic, and DNA-replication programs. 5 Volcano Plots Use plot_gsea_volcano() when positive and negative enrichment should be inspected in one symmetric view. Use plot_gsea_half_volcano() when one NES direction needs a larger directional panel. 5.1 Symmetric volcano # define volcano labels positive_volcano_label_terms <- c ( "cardiac muscle contraction" , "muscle cell differentiation" , "cardiac chamber morphogenesis" , "heart growth" , "heart valve development" ) negative_volcano_label_terms <- c ( "mitotic nuclear division" , "DNA replication initiation" , "mitotic G2/M transition checkpoint" , "centriole assembly" , "ribosome assembly" ) symmetric_volcano <- plot_gsea_volcano ( gsea_results = gsea_cardiomyocyte_vs_mesoderm, label_n = 10 , label_terms = c (positive_volcano_label_terms, negative_volcano_label_terms), contrast_label = "Cardiomyocyte vs. Mesoderm" , label_words_per_line = 3 ) Figure 3. Symmetric GO biological-process GSEA volcano for Cardiomyocyte vs. Mesoderm. NES is shown on the x-axis, adjusted p-value on the y-axis, and point color marks significant positive, significant negative, or non-significant enrichment. 5.2 Directional half-volcano plots positive_half_volcano_label_terms <- c ( "myofibril assembly" , "cardiac muscle contraction" , "cardiac muscle cell action potential" , "electron transport chain" , "muscle cell differentiation" , "cardiac cell development" , "cardiac chamber morphogenesis" , "muscle contraction" , "cardiac conduction" , "heart growth" , "heart trabecula morphogenesis" ) positive_half_volcano <- plot_gsea_half_volcano ( gsea_results = gsea_cardiomyocyte_vs_mesoderm, direction = "positive" , label_n = 10 , label_terms = positive_half_volcano_label_terms, term_groups = positive_term_groups, category_n = 4 , contrast_label = "Cardiomyocyte vs. Mesoderm" ) Figure 4. Positive NES half-volcano for Cardiomyocyte vs. Mesoderm. The enlarged directional view uses the same labeled positive terms as the positive NES waterfall plot. # define negative labels negative_label_terms <- c ( "DNA-templated DNA replication" , "DNA replication" , "cell cycle checkpoint signaling" , "mitotic cell cycle checkpoint signaling" , "ribosome biogenesis" , "recombinational repair" , "DNA replication initiation" , "cell cycle DNA replication" , "spindle organization" ) negative_half_volcano <- plot_gsea_half_volcano ( gsea_results = gsea_cardiomyocyte_vs_mesoderm, direction = "negative" , label_n = 10 , label_terms = negative_label_terms, term_groups = negative_term_groups, term_group_colors = negative_term_group_colors, contrast_label = "Cardiomyocyte vs. Mesoderm" ) Figure 5. Negative NES half-volcano for Cardiomyocyte vs. Mesoderm. The selected terms emphasize DNA replication, checkpoint, and ribosome-associated programs. 6 Comparative NES Scatterplots Use plot_gsea_nes_scatter() to compare the same GO terms across two GSEA result tables. The scatterplots below compare late and early cardiomyocyte differentiation intervals. # define all-quadrant labels all_quadrants_scatter_label_terms <- c ( "mesenchyme development" , "mesoderm development" , "mesodermal cell differentiation" , "myofibril assembly" , "heart process" , "oxidative phosphorylation" , "regulation of nuclear division" ) 6.1 All quadrants # plot all NES quadrants all_quadrants_scatter <- plot_gsea_nes_scatter ( gsea_x = gsea_day9_vs_day6, gsea_y = gsea_day3_vs_day1, x_label = "Day 9 vs. Day 6 NES" , y_label = "Day 3 vs. Day 1 NES" , color_by = "significance" , quadrant = "all" , x_name = "Day 9 vs. Day 6" , y_name = "Day 3 vs. Day 1" , label_terms = all_quadrants_scatter_label_terms, include_nonsignificant = TRUE , equal_axis_limits = TRUE ) Figure 6. Comparative GO biological-process NES scatterplot for Day 9 vs. Day 6 and Day 3 vs. Day 1. The fitted line summarizes the NES relationship across plotted GO terms, while point color indicates whether each GO term is significant in one, both, or neither contrast. 7 Session Info ## R version 4.6.0 (2026-04-24) ##
